title: Simple & Double Pendulum (Chaos)
description: Simulate simple harmonic oscillation, amplitude-period dependence, mechanical energy conservation, and chaotic double pendulum dynamics

variables.l1Desc: Length of the first pendulum rod or string
variables.m1Desc: Mass of the first pendulum bob
variables.theta1Desc: Initial release angle relative to the downward vertical in degrees
variables.l2Desc: Length of the second pendulum rod (double pendulum mode)
variables.m2Desc: Mass of the second pendulum bob (double pendulum mode)
variables.theta2Desc: Initial release angle of the second bob relative to the vertical
variables.dampingDesc: Viscous air drag and pivot bearing resistance in real mode

presets.simpleHarmonicDesc: Small angle approximation where period is independent of amplitude
presets.largeAmplitudeDesc: Anharmonic motion and Borda series period correction
presets.doubleChaosDesc: Highly nonlinear deterministic chaos with extreme sensitivity to initial conditions
presets.invertedInstabilityDesc: High-energy chaotic motion with full 360-degree irregular rotations

formulas.simplePeriod: Natural period of a simple pendulum in small angle regime
formulas.bordaPeriod: Borda's series formula correcting period for large amplitudes
formulas.energy: Conservation of total mechanical energy (potential + kinetic)
formulas.lagrangian: Euler-Lagrange equations of motion for coupled rotational systems

realMode.airFriction: Gradual amplitude decay due to aerodynamic drag and pivot friction

guided.step1Desc: Run with 15° release. Observe how period precisely matches the classical 2π√(L/g) formula.
guided.step2Desc: Increase angle to 80° and examine how the true period lengthens beyond the harmonic approximation.
guided.step3Desc: Switch to Double Pendulum mode and observe the colorful fractal-like trajectory trail of the second bob.
